text: German investment in Vietnam reaches $3.7 billion

Around 620 German-invested projects were operating in Vietnam as of August 2026, with total registered capital of $3.7 billion and at least 55,000 direct jobs created, according to a report released recently by the German Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Vietnam (AHK Vietnam).

The "Current Status of German Investments in Vietnam 2026/27" report shows that around 120 German companies operate manufacturing facilities in the country, while hundreds of others are active in trade, services, engineering, consulting and digital industries.

More than 250 German companies operate in sales and services, alongside an expanding presence in software development, technical consulting, engineering services, sourcing and business process outsourcing.
This shift highlights Vietnam's growing role beyond a cost-competitive manufacturing base.
German companies are increasingly locating customer support, technical and service operations in the country to serve regional markets.
Software development, industrial engineering, automation and digital services firms have established teams in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, and Da Nang.
German manufacturers are active in sectors including textiles and garments, chemicals, machinery, automotive components, electronics, medical equipment and consumer goods.
Bosch, Schaeffler, Messer, B. Braun and STADA-Pymepharco are among the notable investors.
The expanded Ho Chi Minh City area remains the largest hub, hosting around 70% of German companies in Vietnam and neighbouring areas.
For manufacturing investments, the south accounts for approximately 58% of identified projects, compared with 25% in the north and 16% in the central region.
The report also points to more flexible investment models.
While 71% of surveyed German manufacturers use company-owned facilities in industrial parks, 27% opt for ready-built factories to accelerate market entry.
This reflects growing interest in connecting with existing industrial ecosystems and improving regional supply-chain efficiency.
